rounds.text: Beryl Securities Ltd is experiencing an explosive fundamental acceleration that the market has not yet priced in, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 136% [E17] and a staggering net profit surge of 314% year-over-year [E46]. This operational momentum is supported by medium-term strength, including 77% 3-year sales growth [E16] and 35% 3-year profit growth [E20], alongside accelerating earnings [E49] that outpace recent price action where profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 29% [E40]. Valuations remain highly attractive, trading at a P/E of 13.8x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 7.68x, both of which sit at a steep discount to sector benchmarks of 18.55x [E6] and 13.35x [E11] respectively. Insider conviction is visibly strengthening as well, with promoters increasing their stake by 8.18 percentage points from 52.41% in Dec 2023 to 60.59% in Sep 2026 [E34]. Conceded: operating cash flow is negative at Rs -4.92 Cr for Mar 2026 [E31], resulting in a heavy cash conversion strain [E30], and the 10-year and 5-year compounded profit growth rates remain subdued at 2% [E18] and 1% [E19] respectively.

Despite top-line expansion, Beryl Securities Ltd suffers from severe cash flow destruction, highlighted by an operating cash flow of Rs -4.92 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -5.06 Cr for March 2026, leading to a catastrophic cash conversion ratio of -15.38x [E30, E31, E32]. This fundamental disconnect between reported profits and actual cash realization undermines the stability of the business. Furthermore, long-term return metrics remain dismal, with a 10-year median return on equity stuck at a meager 3% and recent figures confirming an ROE of just 3.2% alongside a flagged low interest coverage ratio [E13, E26, E43]. Valuation metrics also signal caution, as a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value below the current market price, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -19.3% [E36, E37]. Shareholder returns reflect this underlying weakness, with the 1-year compounded share price growth dropping by -6% while the dividend yield sits firmly at 0.00% [E4, E25]. Conceded: [E14, E15, E16, E17].

The bear highlights severe cash flow destruction and negative operating cash flow for March 2026 [E30, E31, E32], but this ignores an accelerating operational turnaround where recent results score 81 out of 100 with net profit up 314% year-over-year [E51]. Conceded: [E30, E31, E32]. While the bear points to historical low long-term return metrics and a 3% median ROE [E13, E26, E43], current efficiency is vastly superior, boasting an ROCE of 14.19% that soundly beats the sector benchmark of 5.86% and a sector-beating ROA of 5.63% [E8, E10]. The bear relies on a discounted cash flow intrinsic value to claim a negative margin of safety [E36, E37], yet recent performance shows profit growth exceeding 1-year price growth by 29%, signaling that the company is starting to outperform expectations [E40]. The bear cites a 1-year share price drop and zero dividend yield [E4, E25], but misses that insiders are voting with their capital by aggressively increasing promoter holdings to 60.59% in September 2026 from 52.41% in December 2023 [E34]. Conceded: [E4, E25].

The bull points to an accelerating operational turnaround and a strong recent score of 81 out of 100 [E51], but this short-term optimism ignores severe structural cash destruction where operating and free cash flows stood at negative Rs 4.92 Cr and Rs 5.06 Cr respectively for March 2026, dragging cash conversion down to -15.38x [E30, E31, E32]. While the bull dismisses historical returns by highlighting current efficiency metrics such as an ROCE of 14.19% [E10], the filed statements confirm that long-term profitability is anemic, evidenced by a 10-year and 5-year compounded profit growth of just 2% and 1% [E18, E19] alongside a stubbornly low median ROE of 3% across 10, 5, 3, and 1-year horizons [E26, E27, E28, E29]. Conceded: [E34, E40, E51]. The bull relies on profit outperforming 1-year price growth by 29% to suggest expectations are being beaten [E40], yet a reverse DCF demonstrates that the current market price of Rs 27.8 requires an unrealistic 2.9% earnings growth against the 1.0% base case [E38], leaving a negative margin of safety of -19.3% relative to the intrinsic DCF value of Rs 23 [E36, E37]. Finally, the bull cites rising promoter ownership [E34] while ignoring official negative flags that the company maintains a low interest coverage ratio, offers a 0.00% dividend yield, and fails to distribute payouts despite reporting periodic profits [E4, E42, E43].
